subject: Intermittent production desync: client SDK stream boundaries causing partial responses
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@fastkart.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@fastkart.com
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Partial responses and p99 spikes impacting checkout (prod)

Hi Marissa,

We're seeing repeated failures on our checkout live stream between 05:30 and 06:10 PT this morning. A subset of requests return truncated payloads (response stops mid-json) and overall p99 token latency spiked to ~3.2s (typical ~450ms). The errors started after our SDK v1.4.2 rollout to 40% of traffic.

Sample trace attached (sdk_sample_trace.txt) and a short snapshot of the failing requests (fastkart-error-snapshot.json). We can roll back but need to understand root cause quickly — this is affecting checkout conversion.

Can you confirm receipt and next steps?

Thanks,
Elena Park
Head of Platform, FastKart
Attachment: sdk_sample_trace.txt (text/plain)
Attachment: fastkart-error-snapshot.json (application/json)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@fastkart.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 08:29:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Partial responses and p99 spikes impacting checkout (prod)

Elena — thanks for the alert and the artifacts. We've received the traces. Immediate plan:

- I'll open an internal incident and loop engine/SDK leads (cc'd).
- Can you confirm whether rollback to v1.4.1 reduces the failures? If you want we can flip traffic now while we triage.
- We'll prioritize a repro and provide an ETA for a patch or mitigation by EOD PT.

Karthik/vivek/monica: please treat this as high-priority. Initial hypothesis from glance: a client-side stream reassembly edge causing the runtime to stop parsing mid-frame when certain multi-line metadata headers are present.

I'll update Elena with the triage notes as they come in.

—Marissa
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0164
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Partial responses and p99 spikes impacting checkout (prod)

Marissa — digging into the attached trace. Quick notes:

- Repro found locally using customer payloads: when the client SDK sends a multi-line custom-metadata header (line-wrapped at ~1024 bytes) the server-side streaming parser treats the following chunk boundary as payload rather than header continuation in ~0.6% of cases. That leads to the runtime closing the response stream early, producing a truncated JSON body on the client.

- Root cause appears to be an SDK framing helper that uses a heuristic to trim CRLF sequences in place; for line-wrapped headers the helper sometimes collapses the CRLF+whitespace into a single newline which interacts badly with our parser's boundary detector. The parser expects exact CRLF sequences for header continuation.

- Short-term mitigation: drop the client-side header continuation heuristic (v1.4.3 hotfix) OR add a server-side tolerant path that accepts folded headers for a short window. I favor the hotfix in the SDK to avoid long-term ambiguity.

- I attached a small repro script (repro-script.py) that demonstrates the failure pattern against our staging endpoint.

Next steps:
1) Push an SDK hotfix branch with the header-preserve change and run canary for 1 hour.
2) If canary is green, coordinate a quick 10% traffic rollout.
3) We prepare a short statement for FastKart with the root cause and ETA (3-6 hours for patch and canary).

—Karthik
Staff Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: repro-script.py (text/x-python)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Escalation: FastKart production impact — executive brief

Aditya — looping you in due to customer business impact and potential SLA exposure. Quick summary:

- What: FastKart seeing truncated streaming responses + p99 latency spike after SDK v1.4.2 rollout to 40% of traffic.
- Impact: checkout failures, measurable conversion drop for a subset of customers.
- Root cause (prelim): client SDK header reassembly heuristic + server streaming parser strictness leading to stream desync in ~0.6% of requests for certain header shapes.
- Proposed immediate action: SDK hotfix (v1.4.3) to preserve header CRLFs and a 1-hour canary. If we need time we can also enable a server tolerant-mode flag for affected customers but that's higher risk.

Requesting:
- Approval to cut and ship SDK hotfix and initiate canary now.
- Guidance on whether Legal/Support should issue a formal incident notification to the FastKart exec sponsor.

I will notify FastKart with the root-cause + ETA within the hour.

—Marissa
From: Elena Park <elena.park@fastkart.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@fastkart.com, Samir Shah <samir@platformops.io>
Date: Mon, 23 Jul 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Partial responses and p99 spikes impacting checkout (prod)

Marissa — thank you for the quick triage and the clear plan. We rolled back our client rollout to v1.4.1 at 09:00 PT on Friday and failures abated immediately.

Please provide ETA for the SDK patch and canary timeline so we can plan a controlled roll-forward. Our renewal conversation is coming up next quarter; we need confidence this won't recur.

Elena Park
Head of Platform, FastKart
